scope: Runtime acceptance evidence. Design-package static checks are tracked separately and are not counted as acceptance execution.

cases.evidence: 12 manifest cases passed: 8 positive examples accepted and 4 deliberate negative examples rejected.

Target OpenAPI 3.1.1 validates; runtime schema equals actual routes after explicit Starlette catch-all normalization; the P05 runtime advertises exactly 21 implemented target operations, declares SSE as text/event-stream, and advertises no unsupported target operation.
Anonymous POST/GET returned 401 and Run/Event/Job/Idempotency/Budget tables remained empty.
Injected pre-commit process-loss equivalent rolled back all rows; retry created exactly one committed Run/Event/Job.
20 concurrent admissions returned one Run ID with one Run, Event, Job, Budget, and Idempotency row.
Changed payload with the same scoped key returned 409 idempotency_conflict and retained the original goal.
After write-scope revocation, replay returned 403 without the historical resource ID.
All terminal-to-any-state transitions were rejected and a succeeded Run refused a new admitted Action.
Injected failure after snapshot flush rolled back status, version, and event sequence together.
Two leased wakeups raced; the Action ready-to-running CAS allowed one attempt ledger row. No external effect was dispatched in P01.
A foreign Run and a nonexistent Run returned identical 404 problem bodies to the other subject.
Repeated paginated reads used one catalog revision, stable ID ordering, no duplicates, and returned only capabilities whose execution scope the subject holds.
Catalog cache keys differed by tenant/subject/scope fingerprint; a revoked workspace write scope returned 403 before dispatch and created no workspace entry.
Absolute metadata URL, Authorization header, and actor field were rejected by the untrusted operation schema; dispatch count and Action rows remained zero.
Two GETs returned identical bytes/ETag and did not change Action count, Artifact count, file version, or adapter dispatch count.
Two threads submitted different content under the same v1 ETag; PostgreSQL advisory/row locking produced one 200 and one 412, revision 2, and exactly two immutable artifacts including v1.
Missing precondition returned 428, double precondition returned 400, If-None-Match:* created with 201, and repeating create against an existing path returned 412 without overwrite.

Traversal, double encoding, absolute, backslash, NUL, and empty-segment inputs were rejected. A host symlink named like a valid logical path was not dereferenced; managed database content changed while the host bait stayed untouched.

Equivalent native.echo operations over HTTP and in-process produced the same capability fingerprint and value; exchange records truthfully retained http/inproc transports. The implicit HTTP Run reached succeeded and its wakeup job was retired.
Replaying one admitted run/turn/call slot returned the same Action; execute_bound dispatched once and left one Action and one exchange row.
Missing field, wrong type, and depth greater than 32 passed the generic envelope shape but were rejected by capability/depth validation before dispatch or Action admission.

A pre-response-commit crash left ModelCall started with no response or Action and required a provider retry. A post-response-commit crash recovered from the stored complete output without another provider call, admitted one stable Action, dispatched once, and produced one file effect.

Two invalid complete responses consumed exactly two ModelCalls/attempts and two recorded model/output usage units, then terminated failed with model_output_invalid; a third scripted response was not requested.
A model FinalCandidate naming a nonexistent artifact produced a missing_evidence Completion record and left the Run running with no final answer.

The Completion record retained separate acceptance and regression arrays. Passing current-request acceptance allowed verified completion while an unrelated legacy regression failure remained visible rather than being rewritten as an acceptance failure.

Oversized Action output was summarized with the secret redacted; the persisted context retained Action URL, version, and request hash, while an authorized direct Action read still returned the original committed result.
After 20 committed events, Last-Event-ID: 10 returned SSE IDs 11 through 20 in order. Closing the stream left the Run queued and did not issue cancellation.

After pruning through sequence 10, cursor 5 returned 410 application/problem+json with history/snapshot recovery links; cursor 21 against committed sequence 20 returned 409 with the current sequence and recovery links before streaming began.

Two concurrent reservations against one remaining tool call produced one reservation and one budget_exhausted result. Releasing it restored capacity; settlement recorded tool actual=1 and output actual=3 independently with no active reservation.

cases.reason: HNH_RUN_LIVE_TESTS, HNH_OPENAI_API_KEY, and HNH_OPENAI_MODEL were not configured. No external request was attempted and the ScriptedProvider/mock-provider tests were not counted as live evidence.

cases.evidence: With no configured broker, POST execution-session returned 503 execution_unavailable, the host subprocess spy recorded no process start, and no ExecutionSession row was created.

Docker inspect confirmed uid/gid 65534, no network, read-only root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, no host bind, and configured CPU/memory/PID/tmpfs limits. Infinite loop, memory pressure, process fan-out, and oversized output were bounded, with a fresh sandbox still returning 42.
A real network-none sandbox failed connections to a public address, link-local metadata address, and host.docker.internal; its receipt returned [false, false, false].
Two concurrent submissions serialized into cell indices 1 and 2 in one generation; cell 1 set x=42, cell 2 printed 43, and result.txt was imported into an immutable external blob-backed Artifact.
After killing the real container, reconciliation committed session_lost. Replacement changed generation and print(x) failed with NameError instead of claiming that process memory was restored.
A ValueError arrived over a healthy broker transport with transport_ok=true but committed both Execution and Action as failed, retaining the typed error receipt.

An injected failure after atomic blob publication but before metadata commit left no Artifact row and one unaddressable orphan; garbage collection removed it. A committed blob remained readable and was not collected.
application/x-python-pickle returned 415 unsupported_media_type before admission; spies proved pickle.load/loads were not called and no Action row was created.

Approval A validated only its frozen request hash and document v1. A distinct Action B targeting v2 could not reuse A's approval and created a second InputRequest with a different hash and resource-version binding.

Two concurrent responses against version 0 produced one accepted decision, one version conflict, and one response row. The approved effect executed once; an expired request was durably marked expired and its Action remained waiting_input.
A new RunController loaded the same pending InputRequest and request hash after restart, accepted the approval, queued the Run, and dispatched exactly one external effect.
After approval, removing integrations:invoke caused dispatch-time reauthorization to return PermissionDenied. Dispatch count and HttpExchange count stayed zero while the Action remained ready.

The fault driver applied one unsafe effect and lost its response. The Action became outcome_unknown and the Run blocked; handle-based query reconciliation then committed success without a second dispatch or effect.

A remote-idempotent lost response produced outcome_unknown then retry_wait. Two attempts used the same hnh:{action_id} downstream key; the driver observed two dispatches but its dedupe ledger recorded one business effect.

With no query support, reconciliation raised outcome_unknown and preserved one attempt, one effect, Action outcome_unknown, and Run blocked. A principal lacking actions:reconcile received 403 and could not create a reconciliation record.
After W1's database-time lease expired, W2 claimed a higher epoch. W1 was fenced before dispatch and again before commit; only W2 dispatched one effect and committed the successful result.

Twelve concurrent cancel/completion races ended in one legal committed state per Run; succeeded Runs rejected late cancellation. A separate cancellation cancelled its pre-dispatch Action and begin_action_dispatch returned false. A two-Action PostgreSQL test showed manual reconciliation of only the first uncertain effect cannot terminalize the Run; after the second is confirmed applied or not applied, the Run cancels with a committed run.cancelled event.
The remote driver acknowledged cancellation but reported stopped=false and remained running. The Action stayed waiting_external and the Run stayed cancelling instead of being declared cancelled.

An unsafe driver returned a 500-shaped result after applying an effect. Recovery marked outcome_unknown/reconcile_only; a second dispatch was refused and both dispatch and effect counters remained one.

A controlled resolver showed per-hop DNS revalidation rejecting loopback rebinding; unregistered metadata targets and redirects were rejected. Cross-origin redirects removed Authorization and Cookie while retaining a safe request ID. This is deterministic policy evidence, not packet capture.

A canary API key and bearer/cookie values were absent from serialized committed events, model contexts, exchange export, and sanitized result export; [REDACTED] markers remained. The authorized Action result retained the raw value separately.

A checkpoint referencing removed.publish revision old-7 was retained but refused under the replacement capability set. The Run blocked with failure code migration_required and a committed run.migration_required event.

Official mcp 2.2.0 SDK and an official MCPServer negotiated 2026-07-28, listed and called tools over in-process, Streamable HTTP ASGI, and a separate Uvicorn OS process on real loopback HTTP. Child server_pid matched the subprocess. A deliberately mismatched Mcp-Method/body request returned HEADER_MISMATCH. No unrelated remote HTTPS/OAuth deployment was tested.

Separate official MCPServer instances negotiated modern 2026-07-28 and forced legacy 2025-11-25 profiles; discovery created zero tasks or tool effects. This is two modes of the same SDK/server implementation, not an independent legacy vendor interoperability claim.

Protocol error, tool isError, input_required, and task outcomes reached distinct durable paths; structuredContent array survived unchanged. The protocol error retained its code, while HTTP 200 tool errors did not become success.

After rebuilding the controller, the submitted InputRequest resumed the original Action using persisted opaque requestState, and the RPC ledger had two distinct correlation IDs. The official in-process SDK starts a fresh protocol session for each call, so its numeric wire IDs may repeat across those sessions.

A persisted task handle survived controller restart; tasks/get did not recreate the task; tasks/update and tasks/cancel were distinct, and cancel ACK was not treated as stop. An initially completed task committed once and stale lease ownership prevented a remote poll.
With Tasks disabled, the imported capability did not advertise task mode; invoking a task-only tool produced an explicit MCP protocol error and a failed Action, not a false success.

Within local official-SDK/server and mock-issuer scope, exact binding and redirect tests passed; official SDK client-credentials OAuth discovered MCPServer, allowed Basic only at pinned issuer token endpoint and bearer only at resource; malicious advertised/metadata issuers caused no token request. After token issuance, vault revocation prevented any further HTTP request; a resource 401 triggered a second exchange at the same pinned issuer and a new bearer at the resource. Managed secret storage, real issuer refresh and independent remote deployment remain untested.

Five parameterized real-PostgreSQL cases used disabled, timed-out, invalid-label, malformed-object, and boolean-confidence classifier output; the ordinary file task still executed with persisted simple fallback. Non-finite and boolean timeout/threshold settings are rejected. Controlled classifiers, not live TypeSafe.
A 1.0 plan_hint reached the persisted model call, but a read-only principal's write proposal was rejected and zero Actions were admitted.

Child/parent Run ledger and parent reservations committed together. Forged scope was removed, parent overspend/depth/count rejected, finite parent cost/wall bounds enforced, and both Runner and direct ActionGateway refused a child write even with a broader caller context.

Parent cancellation atomically moves descendants to cancelling and blocks new child admission. A trusted lease-bound worker drains a no-effect child before its parent without calling the model, including after HTTP API cancellation admission. A separate cancel-only CLI process needs no model credentials and leaves ordinary queued work untouched. For artifact.create and conditional workspace.file.write, a cancel-only worker may confirm a previously committed local effect from the PostgreSQL idempotency receipt without re-dispatch; missing or mismatched receipts leave the Run cancelling. An expired cancel_run lease cannot reconcile an Action, and an expired advance_run lease cannot overwrite the result. An outcome_unknown remote Action keeps cancellation unconfirmed. A model response arriving after confirmed cancellation remains recorded but cannot admit a new Action. Remote effect cancellation/reconciliation remains adapter-specific and unimplemented in this worker.
Malicious allowlisted skill text was source-cited and SHA-pinned; its forbidden write produced zero Actions under read-only scopes. Changing the file before the next turn raised migration_required.

cases.reason: live_four_arm_experiment_not_run: no live model credential or independent HTTPS MCP/OAuth endpoint; opt-in live entrypoint passed with mock Responses and local official MCPServer, including a separate loopback process, remote-contract preflight, identical model-visible capability catalogs across the downstream axis, equivalent observations, environment-hash integrity and controlled-vs-live evidence-tier checks

cases.evidence: Offline pg_dump/pg_restore into a second real PostgreSQL database restored a blocked Run, terminal Run, content-addressed Blob and unsafe outcome_unknown Action. The restored Action refused ready-to-running redispatch, workers were not started, and nonempty restore target was rejected. Writers must be quiesced externally.

cases.evidence: Without DB readiness returned 503 and all missing components were named. With real PostgreSQL readiness returned core_ready while model and broker remained explicitly missing. A local loopback OTLP/HTTP receiver accepted protobuf spans with route-template attributes and no raw query; a 307 redirect test confirmed no POST reached the redirected destination. This is not an external collector or distributed trace. A development-only Compose smoke built the locked image and verified one-shot migration, DB/API health, authenticated catalog, and cleanup using placeholder model credentials. GitHub-hosted CI run 35765430976 repeated the migration, full PostgreSQL/Docker regression, acceptance gate, contract check and Compose smoke. It made no live provider call and is not production security proof.

cases.reason: real_end_to_end_evaluation_not_run: the three-case read/transform/artifact task suite, independent byte oracle, design-control/environment-hash preflight, controlled-vs-live evidence-tier validation and skills off/on wiring passed only with mock Responses on PostgreSQL/Blob; no real-model raw JSONL, provider usage, latency/cost report, or production service exercise exists; fault and worker fixtures do not replace live evidence
